title: Vibrating Screen
model_title: Inclined Vibrating Screen (Double Deck, Circular Motion)

introduction.definition: A vibrating screen separates particles by size. An inclined deck (or decks) of wire mesh, polyurethane or perforated plate vibrates in a circular motion produced by an exciter shaft. Particles smaller than the openings pass through; larger ones travel over the deck and leave at the discharge end. Multi-deck screens make several products at once.
applications: Sizing coal and ore after crushing
key_points: Each deck gives one cut size
Efficiency falls with overload or blinding
introduction.summary: An inclined vibrating screen sorts material by size. An exciter with unbalanced weights makes the screen box move in a circle; particles jump along the decks, and those smaller than the openings pass through. The top deck retains oversize, the bottom deck middlings, and fines fall through both.

foundation: Mount on a structure stiff enough that its natural frequencies are well away from the screen running speed (resonance check by the structural engineer).
alignment: Set the screen to the design inclination and level it side-to-side so material spreads across the full width.
Check spring heights are equal; tension the screen media evenly (side-tensioned cloths) or bolt modular panels correctly.
piping: Feed box/chute should spread the feed across the full width and drop it with low velocity; fit flexible dust seals between the vibrating body and fixed chutes.
Provide spray water headers for wet screening where needed.
commissioning: Run empty and measure stroke/amplitude and stroke angle (stroke card) at all four corners; check for rocking.
Check direction of rotation, bearing temperatures and the time to stop through resonance.

routine.task: Check media for holes and blinding; check feed distribution.

periodic.task: Measure stroke; check springs and bolts; check bearing temperatures.

overhaul.task: Replace screen media, side liners and exciter bearings.

lubrication: Exciter bearings: oil/grease to maker's schedule (critical — high speed, high load).

remedies: Use anti-blinding media, sprays, change opening shape

causes: Impact at feed point, wear, poor tension
remedies: Replace; fit impact plates; tension correctly

safety: Lock out before media change; beware of the body moving on springs during start/stop (resonance).

script.narration: This module introduces the Vibrating Screen.
A vibrating screen separates particles by size.
An inclined deck (or decks) of wire mesh, polyurethane or perforated plate vibrates in a circular motion produced by an exciter shaft.

script.narration: How the Vibrating Screen works.
Feed enters the top of the inclined deck through the feed chute.
The exciter shaft with unbalanced weights makes the body vibrate in a circle.
Particles are thrown and stratify; fines pass through the openings of each deck.
Oversize leaves over the top deck, middlings over the lower deck, fines through the bottom.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Vibrating Screen — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vibrating Screen.
Check media for holes and blinding; check feed distribution.
Measure stroke; check springs and bolts; check bearing temperatures.
Replace screen media, side liners and exciter bearings.
Watch for blinding/pegging: fines in oversize, falling capacity. Common cause: wet or near-size material.
Watch for torn media: oversize in fines product. Common cause: impact at feed point, wear, poor tension.
Watch for bearing failure: high temperature, noise. Common cause: lubrication fault, contamination.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
